A rally in technology companies lifted stocks ahead of results from industry giants valued at more than $10 trillion, with traders also bracing for the Federal Reserve rate decision.
Despite losses in most of its companies, the S&P 500 advanced. A closely watched gauge of chipmakers climbed 2%. Meta Platforms Inc.’s $25 billion stock sale was said to have attracted demand for about five times the available shares. Brent crude dropped below $115. Treasuries wavered.

Bond investors are growing skeptical that the potential return of gridlock on Capitol Hill will ease their worries about the US fiscal trajectory the way it has for decades.
Polls suggest that political outcome is likely once again from US midterm elections on Nov. 3. Democrats are projected to wrest control of at least one chamber of Congress from the Republican Party, while falling short of gaining enough seats to override President Donald Trump’s veto power.

By Rachel PhuaOctober 26, 2026 at 8:43 PM UTCUpdated on October 27, 2026 at 2:27 PM UTCBookmark
Save
Whirlpool Corp. slashed its full-year outlook for the third time this year and forecast its first annual loss in decades, citing a sluggish consumer environment and high commodity prices.
Whirlpool now expects ongoing loss per share of $1.30 for 2026, down from its previous forecast of ongoing earnings per share of $2.50 to $3. The original guidance provided in January was for ongoing EPS of $7.

item.title: Hilton Dips, JetBlue Rallies | Stock Movers
item.description:
Oct 27th, 2026
Hilton Dips, JetBlue Rallies | Stock Movers
Today's biggest winners and losers in the stock market.
On this episode of Stock Movers:
- Hilton Worldwide (HLT) is falling after the hotel operator gave a forecast for adjusted earnings per share for the fourth quarter that fell short of the average analyst estimate.
- JetBlue (JBLU) shares are rallying after the carrier reiterated its expectation to deliver at least $1 in earnings per share and positive free cash flow in 2028. The shares closed Monday at a record low as the airline grapples with cash burn and elevated oil prices.
- Boeing (BA) shares are on the move after posted a quarterly loss after higher costs affected its commercial-jet business. The company's total revenue grew about 4% to $24.19 billion, driven in part by stronger sales from its defense, space and security business. Boeing generated cash despite the loss, and its 737 program is progressing toward stabilized production at 47 jets a month.

Meta Platforms Inc.’s upsized $25 billion share sale attracted demand for about five times the available shares, according to people familiar with the offering, as the company seeks to raise $98 billion for its AI spending.
More than half of the shares in the common stock offering were allocated to long-only and existing investors, said the people, who asked not to be identified because the information is private. The investors taking the 15 largest stakes in the offering accounted for about 70% of the shares, the people said.

Quorum Health, a troubled for-profit chain of rural hospitals backed by private equity firm GoldenTree Asset Management, plans to finance its conversion to a nonprofit with a $1.3 billion bond sale next month.
The network moved one step closer to proceeding with the debt issuance by obtaining the final state approval necessary for the transaction. Quorum operates 11 hospitals in nine states including New Mexico, California and Oregon.

By Eleanor ThornberOctober 27, 2026 at 2:19 PM UTCBookmark

European farmers are curbing fertilizer purchases as elevated prices depress demand, potentially putting crop yields at risk.
Nitrogen fertilizer purchases are running as much as 20% below levels normally expected at this point in the season, according to a market survey by price-reporting agency ICIS. Demand for phosphate, a key nutrient used to support plant growth and root development, is down by 30% or more, some estimates show.

item.title: Brazil Court Probes Foreign Support for Bolsonaro Campaign
item.description: A Brazilian Supreme Court justice ordered federal police to open a probe into possible foreign interference in the country’s presidential election, including potential funding for defeated candidate Flávio Bolsonaro’s campaign.

item.title: UPS Raises Sales Outlook Ahead of Holiday Season
item.description: United Parcel Service raises its sales outlook saying it expects a strong holiday shipping season. The courier raised prices, but demand was still high for the quarter. Earnings and revenue in the third quarter both beat Wall Street estimates. Bloomberg's Matt Griffin reports. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: GM to Leave NYSE for Stock Listing on Tech-Focused Nasdaq
item.description: General Motors Co. plans to shift its stock listing to the Nasdaq Global Select Market from its longtime home on the New York Stock Exchange, an attempt to position the old-school automaker as a tech-forward company embracing automated driving and electric vehicles.
